title: How BlackRock Builds Custom Knowledge Apps at Scale — Vaibhav Page & Infant Vasanth, BlackRock

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk describes BlackRock's Kubernetes-native AI framework (sandbox and app factory) that serves as a platform for other teams to build and deploy custom knowledge apps. The framework targets investment operations workflows in a financial services firm and functions as an internal developer platform. The talk covers app development via the sandbox, deployment through the app factory, and production operations with human-in-the-loop and layered security. Requires familiarity with Kubernetes, LLM strategies, and financial instrument domain knowledge. A conference presentation with live sandbox demonstrations and Q&A. All evidence anchors are directly cited from the transcript with specific character offsets.

summary:
BlackRock, the world's largest asset management firm, has built a modular, Kubernetes-native AI framework to scale custom Knowledge Apps across the enterprise. Infant Vasanth and Vaibhav Page explain how investment operations teams serve as the backbone for portfolio managers, handling data acquisition, trade execution, compliance, and post-trading activities. These teams need internal tools built quickly for complex domains. AI applications at BlackRock fall into four categories: document extraction, complex workflow automation, Q&A/chat systems, and agentic systems. A key use case is the New Issue Operations team, responsible for setting up securities in internal systems when market events occur such as IPOs or stock splits. This requires ingesting prospectuses or term sheets, running them through pipelines, consulting domain experts, and integrating with downstream applications. Agentic systems were tried but do not currently work for this use case due to complexity and domain knowledge required.

Scaling AI knowledge apps presents three major challenge categories. First, prompt engineering requires extensive iteration with domain experts; prompts grow from a couple of sentences to three paragraphs describing complex financial instruments, and teams need versioning, comparison, and evaluation capabilities. Second, LLM strategy selection is complex: choosing between RAG, chain-of-thought, or in-context approaches depends on document complexity, with some documents spanning thousands or even 10,000 pages, exceeding million-token context limits. Third, deployment challenges include distribution, access control, federation, cluster type selection (GPU-based inference versus burstable clusters depending on workload), and cost controls.

BlackRock's framework addresses these through a sandbox and app factory architecture. The sandbox federates bottlenecks such as prompt creation, extraction templates, LLM strategy selection, extraction runs, and logic building directly to domain experts, dramatically accelerating iteration. The app factory is a cloud-native operator that takes a definition and spins out production apps. This approach compressed app development from 3-8 months to a couple of days. The sandbox supports extraction template configuration with field definition, QC checks, validations, constraints, and interfield dependencies. Beyond extraction, the framework includes document management with tagging, labeling, and embedding, plus a low-code/no-code framework for building transformation and execution workflows so operators can create end-to-end pipelines without manual CSV/JSON downloads. The app factory packages all sandbox artifacts into custom end-to-end applications where end users simply upload documents and run extractions.

Key takeaways include investing heavily in prompt engineering skills for domain experts, educating the firm on LLM strategies, evaluating ROI against off-the-shelf products, and designing for human-in-the-loop first in regulated environments where four-eyes checks are required. The framework employs layered security controls across infrastructure, platform, application, and user levels, and uses multiple model providers and strategies depending on the use case.

sections.title: Introduction to BlackRock's AI Initiatives
sections.summary: Infant Vasanth and Vaibhav Page introduce themselves as part of BlackRock's data teams. BlackRock is the world's largest asset manager where portfolio managers synthesize daily information into investment strategies. Investment operations teams are the backbone handling data acquisition, trade execution, compliance, and post-trading activities, requiring complex internal tools built quickly.

sections.title: Classifying AI Applications
sections.summary: AI applications at BlackRock fall into four buckets: document extraction (entity extraction), complex workflow automation, Q&A chat systems, and agentic systems. Each domain presents opportunities to leverage models and LLMs to augment or supercharge existing systems.

sections.title: Use Case: New Issue Operations
sections.summary: The New Issue Operations team sets up securities in internal systems when market events occur (IPOs, stock splits). The process involves ingesting prospectuses or term sheets, running pipelines, consulting domain experts across equity and ETF teams, producing structured output, and integrating with downstream applications. Agentic systems were tried but do not currently work due to complexity and embedded domain knowledge.

sections.title: Challenges with Scaling AI Knowledge Apps
sections.summary: Three categories of challenges: (1) Prompt engineering iteration with domain experts, where prompts grow from sentences to paragraphs; requires versioning, comparison, and evaluation. (2) LLM strategy selection between RAG, chain-of-thought, or in-context approaches depending on document complexity; some documents reach 10,000 pages exceeding million-token limits. (3) Deployment challenges including distribution, access control, federation, cluster type selection (GPU inference vs. burstable), and cost controls.

sections.title: Architecture of BlackRock's AI Framework
sections.summary: BlackRock's framework features a sandbox and app factory on top of data and developer platforms. The sandbox federates bottlenecks (prompt creation, extraction templates, LLM strategy, extraction runs, logic building) to domain experts for fast iteration. The app factory is a cloud-native operator that takes a definition and spins out apps. This compressed app development from 3-8 months to a couple of days.

sections.title: Demonstration of the Sandbox
sections.summary: Vaibhav demonstrates the sandbox's extraction template configuration. Beyond basic prompt and data type management, operators can configure QC checks, validations, constraints, and interfield dependencies. A sample template shows fields (issuer, callable, call price, call date) with field name, data type, source (extracted or derived), required flags, and dependencies, such as callable bonds requiring call date and call price values.

sections.title: Demonstration Continued: Document Management and Low-Code Workflows
sections.summary: After extraction template setup, the demonstration covers document management where documents are ingested from the data platform, tagged by business category, labeled, and embedded. Operators then run extractions and review values. A key improvement over past tools is a low-code/no-code framework enabling operators to build transformation and execution workflows, eliminating the manual process of downloading CSV/JSON files and pushing results to downstream processes.

sections.title: Key Takeaways and App Factory Overview
sections.summary: Three key takeaways: (1) Invest heavily in prompt engineering skills for domain experts, especially in financial services where describing documents is hard. (2) Educate the firm on what LLM strategies mean and how to select them for particular use cases. (3) Evaluate ROI carefully—determine whether building a custom AI app is worth it versus an off-the-shelf product. Additionally, human-in-the-loop is essential in regulated financial environments requiring four-eyes checks. The app factory packages sandbox artifacts (extraction templates, transformers, executors) into custom end-to-end applications where end users simply upload documents and run extractions without worrying about configuration or integration.

sections.title: Q&A Session
sections.summary: Audience questions address feature transformation from document-level metrics to executive-level analytics, information extraction boundaries, and error prevention. Presenters clarify the framework targets investment operations domain experts specifically, not executive-level analytics. Security is layered across infrastructure, platform, application, and user levels with policies across the stack. Multiple model providers and strategies are used depending on the use case, not just a single RAG approach.
